nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a proper metric space (closed balls are compact), $F : X \to \mathbb{R}$ lower semicontinuous and bounded below by $m$, and $h > 0$. Then from every $x$ there is a minimizing-movement step. Proof: $G(z) = \tfrac12 d(x, z)^2 + h F(z)$ is lower semicontinuous, and $G(z) \le G(x) = h F(x)$ forces $d(x, z)^2 \le 2h (F(x) - m)$, so the minimum of $G$ over a compact closed ball is a global minimum.

It is the minimizing-movement step of the free energy in the Wasserstein space, restricted to admissible densities.

This is the implicit Euler scheme for the gradient flow of $F$ written with the distance only: in a Hilbert space with $F$ differentiable, a minimizer satisfies $y = x - h \nabla F(y)$.
